concepts.name: Intuitive idea of a limit
concepts.summary: Explain that a limit describes the value a function approaches as the input nears a point, regardless of the value at the point itself.

concepts.name: Reading limits from graphs
concepts.summary: Estimate limits and one-sided limits from graphs and numerical tables and recognise when a limit fails to exist.

concepts.name: Continuity at a point
concepts.summary: State the three conditions for continuity at a point and identify removable, jump and infinite discontinuities.

concepts.name: Average versus instantaneous rate
concepts.summary: Distinguish the average rate of change over an interval from the instantaneous rate at a point as the interval shrinks.

concepts.name: Derivative as tangent slope
concepts.summary: Interpret the derivative at a point as the slope of the tangent line and as an instantaneous rate of change.

concepts.name: Integral as accumulated area
concepts.summary: Describe the definite integral as signed area under a curve and as accumulated change of a rate.

concepts.name: Derivative and integral notation
concepts.summary: Recognise and read f'(x), dy/dx, the integral sign with limits, and limit notation.

misconceptions.text: The limit of a function at a point is always equal to the function's value at that point.
A limit that approaches a value means the function actually reaches and never passes that value.
A function that is defined at a point must be continuous there.

concepts.name: Limit laws and algebraic evaluation
concepts.summary: Compute limits using limit laws, factoring, rationalising and simplifying indeterminate 0/0 forms.

concepts.name: Limits at infinity
concepts.summary: Evaluate limits as x goes to infinity and infinite limits to find horizontal and vertical asymptotes.

concepts.name: Limit definition of the derivative
concepts.summary: Compute derivatives of simple functions directly from the limit of the difference quotient.

concepts.name: Power, sum and constant rules
concepts.summary: Differentiate polynomials and power functions and the derivatives of sine, cosine and exponential functions with the basic rules.

concepts.name: Product and quotient rules
concepts.summary: Apply the product and quotient rules to differentiate combinations of functions.

concepts.name: Chain rule for composites
concepts.summary: Differentiate composite functions by multiplying the outer derivative by the inner derivative.

concepts.name: Basic antiderivatives
concepts.summary: Find antiderivatives of power, trigonometric and exponential functions and include the constant of integration.

concepts.name: Riemann sums
concepts.summary: Approximate area under a curve with left, right and midpoint sums and connect finer partitions to the definite integral.

misconceptions.text: The derivative of a product is the product of the derivatives.
In the chain rule you only need to differentiate the outer function.
A limit of the form 0/0 is always 0 or always undefined.

concepts.name: Implicit differentiation
concepts.summary: Differentiate relations not solved for y by applying the chain rule to y and solving for dy/dx.

concepts.name: Derivatives of inverse functions
concepts.summary: Differentiate logarithmic, inverse trigonometric and general exponential functions, using logarithmic differentiation where helpful.

concepts.name: Related rates modelling
concepts.summary: Build an equation relating changing quantities, differentiate with respect to time, and solve for an unknown rate.

concepts.name: Curve analysis with derivatives
concepts.summary: Use critical points, monotonicity, concavity and inflection points to analyse and sketch function behaviour.

concepts.name: Optimization problems
concepts.summary: Formulate an objective function with constraints and justify the absolute extremum on a closed or open interval.

concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.summary: Use both parts of the theorem to differentiate accumulation functions and evaluate definite integrals via antiderivatives.

concepts.name: Substitution for integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate indefinite and definite integrals by substitution, changing limits correctly.

concepts.name: Area and volume by integration
concepts.summary: Set up integrals for area between curves and for volumes of solids of revolution by disks, washers or shells.

misconceptions.text: In related rates, you can substitute the instantaneous values of changing quantities before differentiating.
A point where the derivative is zero is always a local maximum or minimum.
After u-substitution in a definite integral, you keep the original x limits.

concepts.name: Formal epsilon-delta limits
concepts.summary: Analyse and construct epsilon-delta arguments to verify limits of simple functions.

concepts.name: Mean Value and Intermediate Value Theorems
concepts.summary: Analyse the hypotheses and conclusions of the IVT, Rolle's theorem and MVT and apply them to prove properties of functions.

concepts.name: L'Hôpital's rule and indeterminate forms
concepts.summary: Recognise indeterminate forms, transform them to 0/0 or ∞/∞, and justify when L'Hôpital's rule applies.

concepts.name: Integration by parts and partial fractions
concepts.summary: Choose among integration by parts, partial fractions and trigonometric substitution to evaluate integrals.

concepts.name: Improper integrals convergence
concepts.summary: Evaluate and judge convergence of integrals with infinite limits or unbounded integrands, including comparison arguments.

concepts.name: Sequence and series convergence
concepts.summary: Analyse convergence of sequences and series via partial sums, geometric and p-series, and the divergence test.

concepts.name: Convergence tests for series
concepts.summary: Select and justify the appropriate test among comparison, ratio, root, integral and alternating series tests, including absolute versus conditional convergence.

concepts.name: Power series and radius of convergence
concepts.summary: Find the radius and interval of convergence of a power series and differentiate or integrate it termwise.

misconceptions.text: If the terms of a series approach zero, the series must converge.
L'Hôpital's rule can be applied to any limit by differentiating the quotient.
The ratio test being inconclusive (limit equal to 1) means the series diverges.

concepts.name: Taylor polynomials and remainder
concepts.summary: Construct Taylor polynomials and evaluate approximation accuracy using remainder bounds.

concepts.name: Taylor series representation
concepts.summary: Judge when a function equals its Taylor series and derive series for standard functions by manipulation.

concepts.name: Uniform convergence and termwise operations
concepts.summary: Evaluate when limits, derivatives and integrals may be interchanged with infinite sums using uniform convergence.

concepts.name: Riemann integrability criteria
concepts.summary: Assess integrability using upper and lower sums and relate continuity and discontinuity sets to integrability.

concepts.name: Proof of the Fundamental Theorem
concepts.summary: Construct a proof of both parts of the Fundamental Theorem using the Mean Value Theorem and the definition of the integral.

concepts.name: Numerical approximation methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate error and convergence of trapezoid and Simpson rules and Newton's method, and choose among them.

concepts.name: Differential equation modelling
concepts.summary: Create models using separable differential equations and interpret solutions, including exponential and logistic growth.

concepts.name: Pathological functions and counterexamples
concepts.summary: Evaluate the limits of intuition using counterexamples such as continuous nowhere differentiable functions and smooth non-analytic functions.

misconceptions.text: Every infinitely differentiable function equals its Taylor series near the point.
A power series can always be differentiated and integrated termwise anywhere, including at the endpoints of its interval.
Every continuous function is differentiable except at isolated points.
